payload.goal: Bind every commit to the initiative that produced it, exactly and at commit time, and spend that primitive on two gaps that share it. Gap 1 (staleness): several initiatives share one worktree and one branch, so any session's push carries other initiatives' commits and their records never learn their work shipped. Gap 2 (review): closing an initiative is today an unconditional append — nothing rechecks that the execution was right, and a reviewer with no diff can only re-read the record's own prose and confirm it. The design split that makes both reliable: RECORD commit-to-initiative (append-only, can never go stale, since a commit's initiative never changes) and DERIVE pushed/merged from git at read time (git is truth for git state; the log is truth for intent).

tasks.title: DECIDE the capture mechanism, the crux of the whole initiative. PostToolUse-on-Bash sees `git commit` and already holds the session pin, so attribution is exact — but it is blind to commits made in a bare terminal. A git post-commit hook catches every commit regardless of author, but sofar installing git hooks is invasive and a terminal commit has no session to attribute to. Judge on what fraction of commits each actually catches, not on elegance; the whole design rests on this being reliable. Log a Decision.

Resolve the record-hygiene D1 collision: git and sofar commands are exempt from the record today, and 1.1 needs `git commit` recorded. Carving it out AMENDS a prior decision — log a Decision that cites D1 explicitly, never a quiet edit to the exemption.

DECIDE what an unattributed commit does (bare terminal, no session, no pin). It must be VISIBLE, never guessed: attributing by file overlap or timestamp produces confident wrong claims, and a wrong "your work shipped" is worse than a silent gap. Pick the surface (doctor finding, digest line, or both).

Back-compat probe, the initiative-lifecycle 1.1 discipline: verify EMPIRICALLY against a published older engine what it does with a commit-attribution event it does not know. Expected: skipped with a warning, degrading safe. Confirm or refute BEFORE designing on top of it.

Event type + payload, in packages/schema/src/ ONLY. Carries the sha; carries NO pushed/merged field — those are derived, never recorded (see the record/derive split in the goal). Deciding the payload is deciding what can never go stale.

Capture at commit time per 1.1, and verify the recorded sha is the commit THIS session just made. Concurrent sessions share this worktree, so a naive `git rev-parse HEAD` after the fact can pick up a peer's commit — prove the race is closed, do not assume it.
Fold: InitiativeState gains the attributed commit list. Unknown/corrupt lines skipped with a warning, never fatal (CLAUDE.md §Engineering conventions).
doctor: commits reachable on the branch that are attributed to NO initiative — 1.3's surface, and the reconciliation path for anything the capture mechanism missed.

Derive pushed/merged at read time with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> <remote ref>` — never record it, since a force-push or rebase would strand a recorded fact instantly. Decide the behaviour when the remote ref is stale, absent, or never fetched: say "unknown", never guess "unpushed".

Digest surface: replace the weak "N events since write-back" staleness hint with the real signal — "N of this initiative's commits reached origin/main via another session's push". This is the payoff the whole initiative is for. Must stay inside the ≤10,000-char SessionStart guarantee.

DECIDE whether PR state is in scope at all. It is the one piece needing `gh` and a network call, and "no sync service" is a guard-rail in CLAUDE.md. Default is OUT until a Decision says otherwise; pushed/merged already carries most of the staleness value without leaving the machine.

DECIDE review granularity and who pays. Phase boundaries fit a session (3-5 tasks, warm memory, cheap fixes); close-only asks one session to audit 25 tasks at maximum surface and coldest memory. Each review costs a real session, so also fix the size threshold below which an initiative pays nothing — blanket application on a 3-task initiative is how this becomes ceremony.

The evidence packet, rendered from the record (a projection — templates dir only): the phase's commit range and diff from Phase 2's attribution, the tasks claimed done, the decisions IN FORCE when that work happened, the rejected approaches, and any guard violations. Without a diff the reviewer re-reads the record's own prose and confirms it — the packet IS the review.

The instruction half: NAME the skills (`/code-review`, `/simplify`) rather than describing bug-hunting in prose — "check for bugs and edge cases" buys a paragraph of reassurance, a named skill buys a real review. sofar ships zero analysis code and makes zero model calls (SPEC §Architectural invariants); it emits the prompt and records the verdict.

The verdict event: what was found, what is still open, and whether surviving findings become tasks in the plan. A review that can only ever emit "looks good" is a rubber stamp — the verdict must be able to be "no".

Keep review DECOUPLED from marking done. If passing the review is what lets a session go home, the reviewing agent has an incentive to pass and will find nothing. Review emits findings; close reads them; they are separate steps.

Mechanical tier at close, no model needed: tasks still pending/active while closing `done`, phases never resolved, tasks claiming files no file_touched event ever saw, guard violations never addressed, a next_action left dangling. This is doctor scoped to one initiative — and the exact mirror of initiative-lifecycle 4.3, which already catches "every phase resolved but the initiative never closed".

The override is an EVENT, never silent. A hard refusal on a solo tool grows a --force and the flag becomes the habit; "closed with 3 tasks pending, overridden" rendered in the digest forever is what keeps it honest.
`dropped` gets the review too — arguably needs it more, since half-built abandoned work is a bigger landmine than finished work, and today `dropped` demands only a prose reason.

docs/SPEC.md is authoritative: the new event types, the record-vs-derive split and why pushed is never recorded, the close-gate semantics, and §Acceptance criteria. No task is done until its criteria pass.

Dogfood the case that prompted this: run the review over a real closed initiative's phases, and confirm a session whose commits shipped inside a peer's push is TOLD so at SessionStart instead of being manually pinged.

payload.because: git is truth for git state; the log is truth for intent. Duplicating the first into the second is how a record starts lying. The whole point of this initiative is a staleness signal a session can trust — a signal built on recorded push state would itself be the next thing to go stale.
payload.chose: Split the model: RECORD commit-to-initiative attribution in the log, DERIVE pushed/merged from git at read time. A commit's initiative never changes, so the recorded half can never go stale; push state changes constantly (force-push, rebase, branch deletion), so recording it would strand a false fact in an append-only log the moment anyone rewrites history.
payload.over: Recording push/merge/PR state as events alongside the attribution — the obvious symmetric design, and the one that silently rots. Also over deriving BOTH halves from git at read time, which cannot work: git has no idea which initiative a commit belongs to, and that is precisely the fact only sofar holds.
payload.rule: Never record push, merge, or PR state as an event — derive it from git at read time. Only commit-to-initiative attribution is recorded.

payload.because: The range design is a heuristic, and its two failure modes are fatal to gap 1. Concurrent sessions share this worktree, so any range contains peers' commits and the file-set filter is a guess that mis-attributes whenever two initiatives touch the same file — which the adjacency data says is the normal case here, not the edge case. And a claim like "this initiative's work is all pushed" cannot rest on a guess: a wrong "your work shipped" is worse than no signal, because it retires a next action that was never done. Separately, closing the range at session end is an off-by-one that would eat the most important commit of every session, since CLAUDE.md mandates write-back BEFORE the final commit.
payload.chose: Attribute each commit individually, at commit time, when the session pin already names the initiative. Exact by construction.
payload.over: Deriving a phase's commits from session-boundary HEAD shas (record HEAD at session start; the range is startHEAD(N)..startHEAD(N+1)) and filtering that range by the initiative's file_touched set. Proposed and rejected inside the same design conversation on 2026-08-13.

payload.because: Same pattern as the SessionStart digest: sofar injects text, the model acts. It keeps SPEC §Architectural invariants intact (zero model API calls) while still buying a real review. The one check with NO substitute is conformance to the record — whether the shipped code honoured the standing constraints and stayed out of the rejected approaches — because sofar is the only thing that holds them; /code-review cannot know a given decision exists.
payload.chose: The review step is instruction text plus a record-derived evidence packet. sofar renders what to review, against which decisions, over which diff — and names the existing skills (/code-review, /simplify) for the code-quality half. The model reaches for those skills; sofar ships no analysis code and makes no model call.
payload.over: Building bug-hunting, edge-case and code-quality analysis into sofar itself — which would duplicate mature tools badly and drag a record-keeper into being a code analyzer, against CLAUDE.md's guard-rails.
payload.rule: The review step names existing skills for code-quality checks and never reimplements them; sofar emits the prompt and records the verdict, never analyses code and never calls a model.

payload.text:
Opened 2026-08-13 from a design conversation; nothing built yet, no code touched. Created with `--no-bind` on purpose: main is bound to drift-certification, which is mid-Phase 4, and binding would have knocked it off the branch that peer sessions resolve through. So this record has NO branch pointing at it — reach it with `sofar switch commit-attribution` (or a dedicated branch) before starting work, or writes will land in drift-certification.

NEXT: task 1.1, the capture-mechanism decision. Everything downstream is mechanical once it is settled, and it is the one place the whole design can fail quietly — if attribution is only mostly right, the staleness signal in 3.2 becomes a confident lie rather than a gap.

Two open questions the conversation raised and did NOT settle, both for 4.1: whether the review runs at phase boundaries or only at close, and the initiative size below which it costs nothing. Cost is the constraint — each review is a real session, so 6 phases is 6 extra sessions.

`sofar new <slug>` binds the current branch by default, silently replacing whatever binding that branch already had. On a repo like this one — where main carries a live initiative and several sessions share the worktree — that knocks the in-flight initiative off the branch peer sessions and hooks resolve through, with no warning. Check `.sofar/bindings.json` before running it; pass `--no-bind` when the current branch is already bound to live work, then reach the new record with `sofar switch <slug>` or a dedicated branch.

payload.because: PostToolUse capture would reintroduce the exact defect record-hygiene D1 exists to prevent: logging git makes the record un-settleable, since the commit OF the record appends an event about committing the record — confirmed empirically in repo.md M2 ("write back, commit, and the tree is dirty again with command_run"). And record-integrity D6 already rejected per-commit attribution outright, because it "needs state the record deliberately does not keep" and time-window attribution misreads interleaved parallel sessions. A trailer is neither: it is not recorded state and not a time-window guess, so it clears both objections while keeping the established principle — read git, never log it. Git notes were rejected as fragile where it matters most: they need their own push refspec, are dropped by most tooling, and a normal clone sees nothing, which defeats the cross-session sharing that is the entire point. Probed on git 2.50.1 before deciding: cherry-pick preserves the trailer, rebase preserves it, and an untrailered commit reads back as empty rather than as a guess — which hands task 1.3 its visible-never-guessed surface for free.
payload.chose: 1.1 capture mechanism: the commit-to-initiative binding lives in a `Sofar-Initiative: <slug>` COMMIT TRAILER, written by the agent at commit time and read back from git with `git log --format='%(trailers:key=Sofar-Initiative,valueonly,separator=%x2C)'`. sofar appends NO event about commits and stores no sha. Ruled by the user 2026-08-13.
payload.over: A PostToolUse hook on `git commit` (the originally planned option, now dead on arrival); a git post-commit hook installed by sofar; git notes; and dropping exact attribution to keep only the branch-level pushed signal record-integrity 4.4 already ships.
payload.rule: The commit-to-initiative binding lives in a `Sofar-Initiative:` commit trailer and is READ from git — never recorded as an event, and never inferred from timestamps or file overlap.

payload.text:
Trailer probe results, git 2.50.1 (Apple Git-155), run 2026-08-13 before D4 was taken. Read incantation: `git log --format='%h|%(trailers:key=Sofar-Initiative,valueonly,separator=%x2C)'`. Always pass `separator=` — bare `valueonly` emits a TRAILING NEWLINE that corrupts any line-oriented parse.

Survival: cherry-pick PRESERVES the trailer; rebase PRESERVES it (rebase is a cherry-pick sequence); a commit with no trailer reads back as an empty field, never as a guess.

KNOWN LOSSY PATH — squash merge. `git merge --squash` writes SQUASH_MSG with each original message INDENTED BY FOUR SPACES, so git's trailer parser does not see it and the squashed commit reads back as empty. Committing with `-m` discards SQUASH_MSG entirely and loses it the same way. The slug text is still present verbatim in the body, so a fallback that scans the body for an indented marker recovers it exactly — still reading git, not guessing. Consequence if unhandled: a squash-merged initiative reads as "not shipped" when it did ship — a FALSE NEGATIVE, which is the safe direction but still wrong. Not an issue while this repo commits straight to main; it becomes one the first time work lands through a squashed PR.

SETTLED AT 1.1 (D4): the binding lives in a `Sofar-Initiative:` COMMIT TRAILER and is READ from git — never recorded as an event, never inferred. That keeps record-hygiene D1 intact (logging git makes the record un-settleable) and clears record-integrity D6, which rejected per-commit attribution because it needed state the record must not keep. sofar stores nothing about commits; git carries the fact and sofar reads it, exactly as it already reads push state.

tasks.title: DECIDE the capture mechanism. SETTLED as D4: `Sofar-Initiative:` commit trailer, read from git, no event. Probed on git 2.50.1 first — cherry-pick and rebase preserve it, untrailered commits read back empty. See repo memory for the read incantation and the squash caveat.

Resolve the record-hygiene D1 collision by carving `git commit` out of the exemption. DROPPED by D4: nothing is logged, so there is no collision to resolve. The exemption stands untouched, which is the point — the whole design exists to avoid amending it.

DECIDE the surface for an unattributed commit (bare terminal, no trailer). The probe settled the hard half — git reads it back as empty, never as a guess — so what remains is purely where it shows: a doctor finding, a digest line, or both. A wrong "your work shipped" is worse than a visible gap.

Back-compat probe for an unknown event type. DROPPED by D4: no new event type is introduced, so there is nothing for an older engine to fail to understand. Older engines simply do not read trailers — they degrade to today's behaviour exactly.

phases.name: Phase 2 — Write and read the trailer

tasks.title: DECIDE who writes the trailer and how it is made hard to forget. The agent must emit it at commit time, so the instruction belongs in the sofar protocol block that every session already receives — but an instruction alone will be forgotten, and a forgotten trailer is a silent unattributed commit. Weigh a `sofar` subcommand that prints the line, a commit template, and a prepare-commit-msg hook. Reliability is the whole design; this is where it actually leaks.

Read path in core/git.ts alongside readGitState: walk commits, parse the trailer, group shas by initiative. Keep the file's standing rule — it reads FILES, no subprocess, inside the 100ms shim budget (speed T2). A `git log` walk is a subprocess and a graph walk, so decide honestly whether this belongs on the hook path at all or only in on-demand commands.

Squash-merge fallback: `git merge --squash` indents the original message four spaces, so the trailer parser reads empty and a shipped initiative reports as un-shipped. The slug is still in the body verbatim — scan for it as a fallback, which is still reading git rather than guessing. Details and the false-negative direction are in repo memory.
doctor: commits reachable on the branch carrying no trailer and no recovered fallback — 1.3's surface, and the honest accounting of what the mechanism missed.

payload.text:
1.1 is settled (D4) and the mechanism is proven on git 2.50.1, not assumed. Still no code written — everything so far is design plus a throwaway probe repo.

NEXT: task 2.1, and it is now the weakest joint in the whole design. D4 makes attribution exact WHEN the trailer is present, but nothing yet makes it hard to forget: a session that commits without the trailer produces a silent unattributed commit, and enough of those turn the 3.2 staleness signal into a lie by omission. An instruction in the protocol block alone will not hold — decide whether a prepare-commit-msg hook, a commit template, or a `sofar` subcommand that prints the line carries it, and pick on how it fails when someone forgets, not on elegance.

Note the tension 2.2 has to resolve honestly: core/git.ts is deliberately subprocess-free because hook shims run inside a 100ms budget (speed T2), and reading trailers means `git log` — a subprocess AND a graph walk. That may mean the per-initiative signal cannot live on the hook path at all, and belongs in on-demand commands instead. Do not quietly blow the budget to get it into the digest.

From here on, every commit in this repo should carry `Sofar-Initiative: <slug>`; this record's own commits are the dogfood.
